correctness.rationale: Rotational symmetry and strict negative type reduce the constant-distance-potential mass-one equation Dw=lambda 1 to three masses. Substitutions x=sqrt(1+u²)-u,y=sqrt(1+v²)-v give H=1+x²+xy+y²-a(x+y)>0, equator mass (x+y)²/(2nH), apex masses (1+y²-a(x+y))/(2H), (1+x²-a(x+y))/(2H). Independently verified normalization, both distance-potential equalities and derivative dp/dy=x(2xy+y²-1)/(2H²) symbolically. If both apices negative, d² term in H decreases their total negative mass and symmetric z=1/a attains C=(a²-1)/(3-a²). For one negative apex, minimizing p over y at sqrt(1+x²)-x and then x at boundary1 gives B=(a+2-2sqrt2)/(2(2sqrt2-1-a)). Verified exact n=4/n=5 sign crossing with monotone C-B derivative, yielding nonattained n=3,4 vs unique symmetric positive-height maximizer n>=5. Finite distance-matrix tests in source verify individual instances, not the continuum optimization.
residual_risks: Optimization excludes u=0/v=0, correctly describes n=3,4 values as unattained suprema.
